thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: surge of CUDA OOMs observed in decode-stream pool (gpu-decode-prod). error_rate=11.8% over 5m. paging runtime oncall. nodes flapping in us-west1. creating incident channel.

maria: i'm up — paging woke me. seeing repeated 'CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY' originating from decode loop on node-11 and node-14. starting triage now.

kevin: joining. i'll monitor infra (autoscaler, node lifecycle). any confirmed service impact yet?

maria: yes — roughly 260 dropped requests in last 12m. Customers on long streaming sessions saw 5xx spikes. suspicious pattern: many streaming calls with enormous max_tokens (some >100k). snippet from logs: 
```
2026-03-15T14:05:21Z node-11 decode_loop.cu:THREAD ERROR CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
payload: {request_id: "r-bc34", customer: "notebookly", model: "redwood-decode-v2", max_tokens: 150000}
GPU mem reported: 15.9GB/16.0GB
```

raj: sounds like runaway generation. do we currently enforce max_tokens upper bound at the gateway? i thought SDKs were supposed to validate.

maria: gateway currently exposes STREAM_MAX_TOKENS header but it's optional; no hard enforcement. immediate mitigation idea: apply a runtime environment override to cap streaming allocations to 2048 tokens and add an early reject with 4xx if client requests exceed that.

kevin: proceed with runtime cap. i'll also temporarily disable autoscale burst for decode pool to avoid flapping new nodes that OOM and create churn.

maria: applying change now: setting STREAM_MAX_TOKENS_RUNTIME_CAP=2048 on decode-pool-us-west1 and performing rolling restart with graceful drains on affected nodes (node-11, node-14). cmds: 
```
kubectl -n decode-pool set env ds/decode-pool STREAM_MAX_TOKENS_RUNTIME_CAP=2048
kubectl -n decode-pool rollout restart ds/decode-pool --grace-period=60
```

deploy-bot: Rolling update initiated for decode-pool-us-west1 (graceful). node-11 cordoned and drained.

kevin: i've set temporary ingress throttling to 7rps/node on the pool to reduce immediate memory pressure.

sophia: tagging for customer communications. customer 'notebookly' reported truncated streams and saw errors around 14:06-14:20 UTC. opening incident ticket INC-2026-198 and notifying their AE.

maria: after cap applied, OOMs drop sharply. node-11 logs show stable memory usage ~8GB. sample: 
```
2026-03-15T14:11:02Z node-11 decode_loop.cu INFO mem_usage 8.3GB/16.0GB
requests_dropped: 4 (post-mitigation)
```

raj: for a short-term safety measure we should also implement a hard clamp in the proxy that returns 413/4xx with an error code like MAX_TOKENS_TOO_LARGE so clients get immediate feedback instead of triggering runtime allocation.

maria: agree. medium-term: gatekeeper in proxy + SDK update + a regression test simulating extreme max_tokens. short-term: runtime cap + ingress throttle + autoscale burst disabled.

kevin: handoff note: i'll be primary for the next 45 minutes to watch for regressions. maria, please include what you changed and where to find logs.

maria: handing off to kevin. Changes: STREAM_MAX_TOKENS_RUNTIME_CAP=2048 applied to decode-pool-us-west1, pool ingress throttled to 7rps/node, autoscale burst disabled. Affected nodes: node-11, node-14 (drained & restarted). Logs: /var/log/decode/node-*/decoder.log and Datadog query: 'service:decode AND env:prod AND message:OOM'.

ops-bot: PagerDuty incident PD-468 created; oncall: kevin. Severity classified Sev2. Linked ticket: INC-2026-198.

sophia: quick customer impact summary for incident report: 'notebookly' experienced ~14% failed streams in 14:06-14:20 UTC window; system-wide transient 5xx spikes observed. After mitigations (runtime cap + throttling) failure rate reduced to <1% by 14:13 UTC.

raj: follow-ups to track:
- RWD-1001: enforce proxy-level hard max_tokens clamp and return standardized 4xx code MAX_TOKENS_EXCEEDED
- RWD-1002: add a streaming regression test that simulates runaway generations and validates memory safety
- RWD-1003: emit 'stream.max_tokens' histogram metric and alert on extreme tails (>95th percentile threshold)

maria: leaving detailed notes in the incident doc and linking logs. handing customer liaison to sophia. stepping offline for short break; kevin will own monitoring.

kevin: monitoring continued. OOM count is now 0/5m; request drops back to baseline. Keeping autoscale burst disabled until proxy clamp is deployed.

deploy-bot: Rolling update completed for decode-pool-us-west1. All pods reported ready.

sophia: customer comms drafted and sent to affected accounts, included timeline and mitigation steps.

kevin: closing on-the-wire mitigation. please add the follow-ups to the postmortem and assign owners. thanks folks :thumbsup:

maria: good recovery. root cause summary for postmortem: lack of hard proxy limits + clients able to request arbitrarily large max_tokens -> streaming path attempted to allocate huge KV caches -> CUDA OOM and node flaps. contributing factor: autoscale burst reattaching nodes without workload isolation.

sophia: postmortem owner: raj. ETA: 48h for draft.

incident-bot: PD-468 acknowledged and downgraded to monitoring. Severity reduced to Sev3. Channel remains open for postmortem notes.
